# Dataset index

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

This index lists every dataset by asset class or subject, with the query methods, shared arguments, and column types. Each dataset links its own page, with its call, arguments, plans, and columns. In the Deephaven IDE, column descriptions show as tooltips. `dm.datasets()` lists every dataset as a table.

<a id="query-methods"></a>

## Query methods

Create a session with `m = dm.MassiveSession()`. A dataset method, such as `m.stocks.dividends()`, returns a query. A query names the data and reads nothing. The methods below read the data and return a Deephaven table.

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `blink()` | The stream as a blink table, which holds only the latest update cycle's rows. |
| `append_only()` | Every row the stream sends after the call, oldest first. |
| `ring(capacity)` | The latest `capacity` rows the stream sends. |
| `last_by(by='Symbol')` | The latest row of each key, by default one row per symbol. |
| `history(start, end=None)` | The dataset's rows over a range of days or of exact times. |
| `fetch()` | A table of every row Massive has now, up to the query's `limit`. |
| `poll(interval)` | A live table that fetches the query again every `interval`. |

<a id="shared-arguments"></a>

## Shared arguments

These arguments follow the same rules on every dataset that takes them. A dataset's page gives what is particular to that dataset and links here.

<a id="symbols"></a>

### symbols

Each symbol is Massive's ticker, spelled exactly:

| Asset class | Ticker |
| --- | --- |
| Stocks | `AAPL`, `BRK.B` |
| Options | `O:SPY271217C00700000`: `O:` and the OCC option symbol |
| Indices | `I:SPX` |
| Forex | `C:EURUSD` |
| Crypto | `X:BTCUSD` |
| Futures | `ESZ6` |

- Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column.
- A live table works as a watchlist. Symbols you add are read, and symbols you delete stop being read.
- A dataset's page says when `dm.ALL` or leaving `symbols` out reads every symbol.
- In text or a list, any other spelling, such as `aapl`, raises `ValueError`, unless the dataset's page says it takes another source's tickers. In a table, that row is skipped and logged.
- To convert another source's tickers, such as Yahoo's `BRK-B`, use `dm.canonical_symbol`.

<a id="start"></a>

### start

The first day or moment of the range. Give `start` and `end` as two dates or two instants.

- A date is text such as `"2025-06-02"`, a Python `date`, or a Deephaven `LocalDate`. It's the day in the market's time zone: New York for stocks, options, and indices, and UTC for forex and crypto. For futures, it's the trading session that ends that day.
- An instant is a Python `datetime` with a time zone, a Deephaven `Instant`, or Deephaven time text such as `"2025-06-02T09:30 ET"`.
- A dataset whose range is a calendar date, such as an ex-dividend date, takes dates only.

<a id="end"></a>

### end

The last day of the range, included, or the instant the range stops, excluded. Give it in the same form as `start`. Leave it out for no end. Rows dated in the future, such as upcoming dividends, then come back too.

<a id="date"></a>

### date

One calendar day, in the same forms as a `start` date.

<a id="as_of"></a>

### as_of

Read the data as it stood on this date. Leave it out for Massive's latest data.

<a id="sort"></a>

### sort

The field to order the rows by, as Massive names it, such as `"ex_dividend_date"`. Each dataset's page lists the fields it takes.

<a id="order"></a>

### order

The direction of the rows: `dm.Order.ASC` or `dm.Order.DESC`. On a dataset with `sort`, give the two together.

<a id="limit"></a>

### limit

The most rows to return. Each dataset's page says whether the limit counts each symbol's rows or all of them. To keep the latest rows, sort newest first, such as `sort="ex_dividend_date", order=dm.Order.DESC`.

<a id="filters"></a>

### filters

Any other parameter Massive documents for the dataset, as a `dict`. Write each dot in a name as `_`: Massive's `strike_price.gte` is `strike_price_gte`. Each dataset's page lists the keys it takes, and any other key raises `ValueError`.

<a id="adjusted"></a>

### adjusted

`True`, the default, adjusts prices and volumes for splits. `False` gives them as traded. Live bars and bars from flat files are always as traded.

<a id="timespan"></a>

### timespan

The unit of each bar, a `dm.Timespan` member such as `dm.Timespan.MINUTE` or `dm.Timespan.DAY`. Futures take `SESSION` in place of `DAY`. On a bars dataset, one-second and one-minute bars with `multiplier=1` also stream. Bars of other lengths are history only.

<a id="multiplier"></a>

### multiplier

How many `timespan` units each bar spans, 1 by default. `timespan=dm.Timespan.MINUTE, multiplier=5` gives five-minute bars.

<a id="venues"></a>

### venues

The futures exchanges whose flat files `history()` reads, as a set of `dm.FuturesVenue` members. The default is all four. Pass the ones your plan includes.

## Column types

Each column has one of these Deephaven types:

| Type | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `double` | A 64-bit floating-point number, Python's `float` |
| `long` | A 64-bit integer |
| `Boolean` | True or false |
| `String` | Text |
| `Instant` | An exact moment in time |
| `long[]` | An array of `long` |
| `String[]` | An array of `String` |

## Columns whose type differs by asset class

These columns have different types in different asset classes of the same dataset, such as `m.stocks.snapshots` and `m.crypto.snapshots`. To merge two such tables, select the same columns from each, then cast one table's column to the other's type, such as `a.update("LastTradeSize = (double) LastTradeSize")`:

| Dataset | Column | Types |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `snapshots` | `LastQuoteBidSize` | long for stocks and futures, double for options |
| `snapshots` | `LastQuoteAskSize` | long for stocks and futures, double for options |
| `snapshots` | `LastTradeSize` | long for stocks, options and futures, double for crypto |
| `snapshots` | `LastMinuteVolume` | double for stocks, options, forex and crypto, long for futures |
| `snapshots` | `SessionVolume` | double for options, long for futures |
| `movers` | `LastTradeSize` | long for stocks, double for crypto |
